A Megalodon is a massive prehistoric shark, the largest predatory fish to ever exist. The body is the classic shark shape: a torpedo-shaped trunk of dense muscle and cartilage, a broad triangular dorsal fin, a pair of long pectoral fins, and a crescent-shaped caudal fin that propels the animal with each sweep. The head is wide and blunt with a jaw large enough to bite a small ship in half. The mouth contains six rows of teeth arranged in a conveyor-belt system: when a tooth in the front row breaks, the next row rotates forward to replace it within days. Each tooth is a triangular serrated blade roughly the size of a dinner plate on an adult, finely notched along both edges, and angled inward so prey cannot pull free once the jaws close. The bite force crushes a whale's ribcage in one snap.

The skin is covered in millions of microscopic tooth-like dermal denticles that overlap in a tight mosaic. Running a hand over the hide from head to tail feels like fine grit stone. Running it the wrong direction tears flesh. The denticles channel water flow to reduce drag and turn aside the claws and teeth of other predators. The dorsal surface is dark slate grey or blue-grey, the ventral surface pale cream or white, a counter-shading pattern that makes the animal difficult to spot from both above and below. The eyes are large, solid black, with a reflective layer behind the retina that amplifies dim light and a protective membrane that slides across the eye during a bite. The five gill slits on each side pump water continuously. At speed the mouth opens slightly and water passes directly through the gills, allowing the animal to breathe without slowing.

Megalodons are solitary and control territories spanning hundreds of square miles of open ocean. They hunt from below, circling in the dark water beneath the thermocline for hours before striking vertically at full speed, often breaching the surface with the prey clamped in their jaws. The initial bite targets the midsection. If the prey survives, the Megalodon circles back and bites again, each pass removing another chunk until the prey bleeds out or sinks. They do not chew. They swallow torn sections whole, each bolus sliding down a gullet wide enough to admit a rowboat. A single adult eats roughly 2,000 lbs of meat per day, hunting whales, giant squid, and large fish. A Megalodon that learns to associate ships with food will target vessels repeatedly. They are not intelligent like a Kraken or Aboleth. They do not plan or hold grudges. Their senses are their main advantage: a Megalodon detects a single drop of blood in the water from over a mile away, senses pressure changes from struggling prey hundreds of feet distant through its lateral line, and tracks the electrical impulses of living hearts and twitching muscles through murky water and seafloor sediment via the ampullae of Lorenzini clustered around its snout.

Megalodons reproduce by live birth. A female carries 2 to 4 pups for 18 months and gives birth in warm shallow nursery waters. The pups emerge at 8 to 12 feet long and are immediately capable predators. The mother offers no care and will eat them if they linger. Surviving pups flee to shallows where adults cannot follow. Siblings do not cooperate. Megalodons gain 1 level per year of life, increasing in size and power as shown in the growth table. They reach sexual maturity at level 15. They continue growing indefinitely and have no known maximum lifespan. The oldest specimens are believed to be several centuries old.

Beyond normal leveling, a Megalodon can evolve into a more advanced form through a growth surge. When a Megalodon reaches the minimum level required for its current stage and successfully hunts and consumes a creature of its own size category or larger, the volume of food triggers a rapid growth state. The Megalodon must make a CON save against the DC for its current type. On a success, its body enlarges over the course of 1d4 hours of continuous feeding, growing into its next evolutionary stage. On a failure, the meal is digested normally and the Megalodon must gain another level before attempting again. A Megalodon mid-surge will attack anything that moves, driven by hunger that overrides its normal caution. The save DC gets higher for more advanced forms, making each growth surge harder to trigger than the last.

The evolution path and minimum level requirements are as follows. A newborn starts as a Pup Megalodon. A Pup cannot attempt a growth surge until level 5, at which point it may attempt to evolve into an Adult Megalodon by consuming a creature of size Medium or larger. An Adult must reach level 15 before it can attempt to evolve into an Elder Megalodon by consuming a creature of size Large or larger. An Elder must reach level 35 before it can attempt to evolve into an Abyssal Megalodon by consuming a creature of size Huge or larger. An Abyssal Megalodon is the final stage and cannot evolve further, but it can continue leveling indefinitely with no maximum level. When an Abyssal Megalodon reaches level 60 or higher and its body begins to fail from age, it may choose to accept its end by sinking to the deepest trench it can find, settling on the seafloor, and stopping. The body dies over several days and becomes the foundation of a deep-sea ecosystem that will persist for decades. This final act is called the Benthis Fall. Fewer than ten Abyssal Megalodons are believed to exist in all the oceans of Eyum.

When killed, a Megalodon can be harvested for hide, meat, blubber, teeth, and bones. The hide is rough leather made of dermal denticles; armor crafted from it resists slashing damage and injures creatures that strike it with bare skin or natural weapons. The meat is dense, red, and nutritious, though it spoils within hours if not salted or smoked. The blubber renders into a clean-burning oil used for lamps and waterproofing. The teeth are serrated blades that hold an edge indefinitely. The bones are dense skeletal material strong enough for tool handles and lightweight weapon components. See [[2.6.2 Animal and Monster Materials]] for crafting stats and pricing.

**Evolution CON save DCs by type**: Pup Megalodon DC 12, Adult Megalodon DC 16, Elder Megalodon DC 24.
###### Variant Descriptions
All Megalodons share the same basic body plan regardless of stage. The stage is determined by age and size, not genetics. A Pup that survives long enough will eventually become an Abyssal if it keeps eating and growing. The stages are as follows.

**Pup Megalodon (DR 2):** The smallest and youngest stage, recently independent from the mother. 10 to 17 ft long, weighing up to roughly 1,000 lbs. The body proportions are leaner than an adult, with a shorter snout and proportionally larger eyes. The dorsal fin is not yet fully rigid and flops slightly when the animal turns sharply. The teeth are about 3 inches along each edge, already fully serrated but still small enough that a Pup cannot bite through a ship's hull. Pups are fast and nervous, fleeing from anything larger than themselves and hunting fish, seals, and small dolphins in the shallows. They are the stage most likely to be encountered near coasts and in warm nursery waters. A Pup cannot attempt a growth surge until level 5. Before level 5, a Pup that feeds on a sufficiently large creature simply digests it with no chance of evolution.

**Adult Megalodon (DR 6):** The classic form, the animal that most people picture when they hear the word Megalodon. 25 to 53 ft long, weighing 8,000 to nearly 25,000 lbs. The body has thickened and the snout has lengthened into the familiar blunt profile. The dorsal fin is fully rigid and stands 4 to 6 ft above the water when the animal surfaces. Each tooth is roughly the size of a dinner plate. An Adult can bite through a ship's hull below the waterline and has the jaw strength to crush a whale's skull. Adults hunt in the open ocean, following whale migrations and patrolling the deep water along continental shelves. They are the stage most commonly depicted in sailor's stories and the one most responsible for the Megalodon's reputation as a ship killer. An Adult must reach level 15 before attempting a growth surge.

**Elder Megalodon (DR 12):** A Megalodon that has survived for over a century and grown past the limits of the adult form. 55 to 123 ft long, weighing 30,000 to over 130,000 lbs. The body is thick and scarred from a lifetime of combat with whales, giant squid, and other Megalodons. The skin is greyed and the denticles are worn smoother in places from age. The dorsal fin is a rigid blade 8 to 12 ft tall, the sight of which will cause experienced sailors to turn their ships around without hesitation. The teeth are massive, the largest exceeding 8 inches along each edge. The jaw strength can snap a ship's keel. Elders are slow compared to younger stages but nearly impossible to kill through conventional means. Their bodies have begun regenerating minor wounds faster than they can be inflicted, and their hide has thickened to the point that most weapons glance off. An Elder must reach level 35 before attempting a growth surge.

**Abyssal Megalodon (DR 22):** The final stage. An Abyssal Megalodon is no longer simply a large shark, it is a geological event. 100 ft and larger, weighing 65,000 lbs at minimum and continuing to grow indefinitely. The body is so massive that its passage through the water creates currents felt by ships on the surface. The skin is nearly black and thick enough to turn cannonballs. The dorsal fin is visible from miles away and is often mistaken for a second ship's sail. The teeth exceed a foot along each edge and are serrated deeply enough to saw through iron. An Abyssal Megalodon does not hunt individual whales. It swallows entire pods. Its jaws can bite a galleon in half. Abyssal Megalodons live in the deepest trenches and rise only rarely, usually when something has disturbed their territory or when the hunger becomes too great to ignore. They are one of the most powerful non-magical creatures in existence. Fewer than ten are believed to be alive. An Abyssal Megalodon cannot evolve further and has no maximum level. At level 60 or higher it may accept its end through the Benthis Fall.
###### Unique Abilities
- **Serrated Maw (Passive):** All stages. The Megalodon's Bite attacks ignore Lesser Resistance to Physical damage. Against creatures with full Resistance to Physical damage, treat it as Lesser Resistance instead. If the Megalodon hits the same creature with a Bite attack two turns in a row, the second Bite deals an additional 1d8 damage as the serrations tear the wound wider.
- **Ampullae of Lorenzini (Passive):** All stages. The Megalodon has blindsight out to 60 ft while submerged, sensing the electrical impulses of living creatures through water. This penetrates murky water, silt, and seafloor sediment but cannot detect creatures with no heartbeat or muscle activity. The Megalodon automatically detects any creature within range not specifically hidden from electroreception and has advantage on attacks against creatures that are [[2.4 Conditions#Physical-Conditions|Bleeding]].
- **Breach (Active, 6 Mana):** All stages. The Megalodon accelerates upward from below, launching its body out of the water. Make a Bite attack against a creature on the surface within melee range. On a hit, the target takes the Bite damage plus an additional 1d10 + [[2.1 Affinities#Attack Damage Bonus|Attack Damage Bonus]] bludgeoning damage from the force of impact and must make a STR save (DC 10 + [[2.1 Affinities#Save DC Bonus|Save DC Bonus]]) or be thrown 20 ft into the air and become [[2.4 Conditions#Environmental / Positional Conditions|Prone]] upon landing in the water. The Megalodon lands back in the water in an unoccupied space adjacent to the target.
- **Death Roll (Active, 5 Mana):** Adult and above. The Megalodon seizes a creature [[2.4 Conditions#Environmental / Positional Conditions|Grappled]] in its jaws and rolls its entire body in a rapid spiral. The target takes 1d12 + [[2.1 Affinities#Attack Damage Bonus|Attack Damage Bonus]] slashing damage and must make a CON save (DC 10 + [[2.1 Affinities#Save DC Bonus|Save DC Bonus]]). On a failure the target gains the [[2.4 Conditions#Physical-Conditions|Bleeding]] condition and takes an additional 1d6 damage at the start of each of its turns for 3 turns or until magically healed.
- **Crushing Jaws (Passive):** Adult and above. When the Megalodon makes a Bite attack against a creature or object of size Large or smaller, the target must make a STR save (DC 10 + [[2.1 Affinities#Save DC Bonus|Save DC Bonus]]) or be [[2.4 Conditions#Environmental / Positional Conditions|Grappled]] in the Megalodon's jaws. A creature [[2.4 Conditions#Environmental / Positional Conditions|Grappled]] this way takes the Bite damage automatically at the start of each of the Megalodon's turns until it escapes. The Megalodon can grapple only one creature in its jaws at a time and cannot make Bite attacks against other targets while doing so.
- **Terror of the Deep (Passive):** Elder and Abyssal only. At the start of combat, any creature of level 10 or lower that can see the Megalodon must make a WIS save (DC 10 + [[2.1 Affinities#Save DC Bonus|Save DC Bonus]]) or gain the [[2.4 Conditions#Mental-Conditions|Frightened]] condition for 2 turns. Creatures that succeed are immune to this effect from that Megalodon for 24 hours. Triggers once per encounter.
- **Shipbreaker (Passive):** Abyssal only. The Megalodon deals double damage to structures, ships, vehicles, and inanimate objects. Ships and structures treat the Megalodon's attacks as if they had AC 5. The Megalodon's Bite attacks ignore the Damage Threshold of objects.

**Standard Passives:** Damage Threshold (Elder and Abyssal only), Hardened Body (Elder and Abyssal only), Pursuer (all stages), Regeneration (Elder and Abyssal only), Anchored Vitality (Abyssal only)
**Standard Actives:** Bite, Charge, Slam, Heavy Strike (Elder and Abyssal only), Breach, Death Roll
